evidence.passage:
## 1. Exact per-P disposition (corrected)

Disposition vocabulary: ALREADY-COVERED (discovery coverage only — no deployment is claimed);
CORRECTION (P text as stated is wrong/unsafe in some respect); OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENT
(recommended extension, adoption conditional); USER DECISION (station must decide; research gives
options + rules, not answers); REJECTED (considered and not recommended, with reasons);
UNCERTAIN (evidence absent/inapplicable/weak, with resolver).

### P1: "Provide a shared show schedule and operator handoff view for both transmitters and the web stream."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED (as discovery coverage only) + CORRECTION (privacy; staleness) +
OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENTS (conditional) + USER DECISION (via P6) + REJECTED (broadcast-stack build).

- ALREADY-COVERED (qualified): discovery establishes the object model — one program/segment
  record feeding a live schedule view plus a per-shift handoff view for studio and web-stream
  operators. The calendar/history shape is corroborated by LibreTime's user-manual model
  (S05, https://libretime.org/docs/user-manual/ — show calendar, playlists and smart blocks,
  scheduling, history) and the multi-output permission shape by AzuraCast's global-vs-station
  permissions (S09, azuracast.com roles-and-permissions doc, dated 2021-02-09). "Covered" means
  the concept is evidenced and specified — no tool has been deployed or passed a station test.
- CORRECTION / privacy: P1 as stated omits the brief's dedication-privacy constraint. A single
  naive "shared view" (one printout, one login, one unfiltered table) violates the brief. The
  handoff view MUST be a redacted projection: dedications isolated (deny-all-non-owner table
  with condition `user.Access != OWNER`, R/U/C/D denied, per S11,
  https://support.getgrist.com/access-rules/) or redacted columns; host Editors WITHOUT the
  document-wide structure permission S (S11 warns S permits formula creation that can expose
  otherwise restricted data); verified per receiving role (revised V1/V2).
- CORRECTION / redaction mechanism (defect admitted and fixed): the draft's "Owner-context job
  enforces the same deny rules" is WITHDRAWN. A Grist Owner can read the protected table, so a
  non-owner denial cannot redact an Owner's print/export — the proposal was internally
  inconsistent (critic sustained; S11 enabled-rules semantics confirm Owners retain full read).
  Replacement, in preference order: (a) a verified NATIVE redacted print/export path exercised
  as the receiving role and checked across rendered print, downloads, HTML, API-visible output,
  formulas/widgets, and copies; or (b) a CUSTOM job with an explicit field allow-list/redacted
  projection plus a restricted receiving-role export, treated as a separately budgeted feature
  with a named implementation owner, credentials, support, and failure modes; or (c) a dedicated
  private store with no handoff joins, if the platform cannot establish a simple redaction
  boundary. No export path is recommended until it passes V1.
- CORRECTION / staleness: P1 must also fix the brief's observed failure (post-print updates
  missed by the web-stream operator). The live view is the authoritative record; every
  paper/export copy shows its last-change time/revision; one feasible signal/acknowledgement path
  covers both transmitters and the web-stream operator (revised V4 with real operators,
  change-to-visible and acknowledgement times recorded; the brief sets no numeric target).
- OPTIONAL (conditional): AzuraCast playlist-priority ordering (S10,
  https://www.azuracast.com/docs/user-guide/playlists/ — post-2024-09-01 numeric priorities,
  default 7..0 table) is an AUTOMATIC-selection semantic; its use as an operator-facing
  insert rule is unproven. Kept as a design analogy/question: ask the station how a late insert
  supersedes a track/segment, then show the chosen rule and reason. LibreTime-style "what aired"
  history (S05) is likewise optional — it creates a distinct record with its own retention need
  and is not folded into the aid by default.
- USER DECISION: P1's "for both transmitters and the web stream" is qualified by P6/D3 for the
  transmitter pair; web-stream freshness stays a P1 matter (see P6 for the separation).
- REJECTED for P1's implementation: building on a broadcast playout stack (LibreTime playout,
  AzuraCast AutoDJ, Rivendell automation). Reasons: the brief's explicit non-goal, the Linux ops
  cliff with no in-house developer (S04 LibreTime install minimums — 1 GHz, 1 GB req/2 GB rec,
  static IP, ports 80/8000/8001/8002; S08 AzuraCast requirements — min 2 GB/20 GB Docker host,
  rec 4 cores/4 GB/40 GB), and budget risk. Planning/permission semantics are adopted; stacks
  are not. Rivendell v4.5.0 (S17, https://www.rivendellaudio.org/ — dedicated Ubuntu 22.04
  appliance, pro audio adapters) is the hardest rejection.

### P2: "Track clearance status and restrictions at the track or clip level used in a show."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED + OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENTS + UNCERTAIN (attachments). The draft's
"CORRECTION" label for the approval workflow is RECLASSIFIED (sustained — P2 is not wrong for
omitting an approver role the brief reserves to P5).

- ALREADY-COVERED: per-segment clearance state with a restriction-note field at track/clip
  granularity. Durable modeling proposal (design inference, not a proved Grist feature):
  distinguish reusable clip/track facts (a clip's general restriction) from airing-specific use
  (a dated use adding context). Never compute a "cleared" default: states are unknown, pending
  review, restricted, or cleared, with station-agreed meanings — silence or missing approval must
  never render as CLEARED, especially while D1 is undecided.
- OPTIONAL (approval scaffold, tied to P5/D1): an approval state machine on usage notes
  (PROPOSED → APPROVED with author + time, where the tool provides them) is recommended but
  remains conditional on the station's D1 decision. Any pilot-time hold (e.g. temporary
  Owner-only review) must be explicit, named, management-approved, and marked temporary — it has
  no brief-based authority and may bottleneck nine staff plus volunteers. Verify in the pilot who
  can actually alter a usage note.
- OPTIONAL (legal-reminder copy): a brief neutral line — "station record, not a license grant" —
  may accompany the status field. The AzuraCast licensing disclaimer (S08 requirements page)
  is not a legal opinion about this station and the status field must never imply software
  verifies a license or grants rights.
- UNCERTAIN (attachments): whether restrictions need file attachments or plain text suffices.
  Resolver: collect five real restriction examples at pilot setup; design attachment storage only
  if examples demand it (storage caps interact: S12 Grist tiers, S16 Baserow tiers).
- Duration arithmetic: the O3.1 regression shape (S02/S03) applies ONLY if the aid computes
  remaining time or auto-fills durations (conditional V3 with the feature's real units, rounding,
  local-break edits, boundaries). A manual rundown with display-only durations marks V3
  inapplicable; LibreTime smart-block semantics must not become a requirement for it.

### P3: "Preserve a printable daily log and a manual fallback for transmission interruptions."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED + CORRECTION (verified redaction path; reconciliation; scope) +
OPTIONAL (dual format).

- ALREADY-COVERED: a redacted, timestamped daily log plus a manual fallback (local single-file
  rundown + USB + paper from one snapshot; TiddlyWiki v5.4.1 single-file model, S19,
  https://tiddlywiki.com/, is one carrier, static export the general one).
- CORRECTION / redaction path: the scheduled Owner-export is replaced per P1 — prefer the
  simplest proven NATIVE print/export path that yields a redacted, version-stamped rundown; if
  none exists, the custom job needs an implementation owner and funded operating cost BEFORE it
  becomes a recommendation. Paper/USB/local copies carry their own access, disposal, and
  freshness risks: deleting a live row does not delete printed/cached copies.
- CORRECTION / reconciliation: the fallback needs a run-and-reconcile procedure — operate from
  the stamped copy during the outage, record changed inserts separately, reconcile into live on
  recovery keyed by the version stamp (revised V7 tabletop).
- CORRECTION / scope ("which interruption?"): "transmission interruption" is ambiguous. This aid
  addresses TOOL/NETWORK unavailability (operator can read a current local rundown without
  app/network, then reconcile). An actual TRANSMITTER/STREAM-path failure is station engineering:
  V7 cannot pass by asserting "show continues" unless station personnel separately exercise
  existing transmission equipment and procedure. Any engineering runbook stays outside the
  product promise; the boundary is stated plainly in the pilot plan.
- CORRECTION / retention surfaces: provider history, backups, exports, and paper are retention
  surfaces to investigate, not automatic conformers to a retention-days setting. Current vendor
  summaries (Grist Pro three-year snapshots per S12/CR-GRIST-PRICE; Baserow Advanced 180-day
  row-change history per S16/CR-BASEROW-PRICE) do not prove whether or how deleted request
  contents remain recoverable — check backup/revision behaviour for deleted values before
  collecting requests, and resolve D2 with management first.
- OPTIONAL: dual-format fallback (paginated print CSS + single-file HTML) from one snapshot.

### P4: "Use text labels with status cues so operators do not rely on color alone."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED, normative MUST for labels; second cue optional redundancy
(corrected from the draft's "label plus cue mandatory" — sustained).

- The brief's label requirement is itself clear and complete. W3C Understanding SC 1.4.1
  (S18, https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html, Level A) requires that
  color not be the only visual means: ONE additional visible indicator suffices, and the
  brief's text label satisfies it. For hue-critical meanings (green-valid/red-invalid — exactly
  this clearance display), the additional indicator is required regardless of contrast; the
  separate 3:1 lightness note does not remove the label requirement (confirmed by
  CR-WCAG-COLOR). Icons/shape/position are recommended redundancy, not a second mandate.
  Labels appear in live, print, and local-export views; print stylesheets must preserve them.
- Acceptance (revised V6): text-only/monochrome inspection of every view PLUS an actual task
  performed by the staff member who raised the need, with status meanings reviewed with them.
  Deuteranopia/protanopia simulation and grayscale review are supporting evidence, not
  acceptance by themselves. Screen-reader semantics may be proposed separately; they are not
  implied by the stated color-perception need and no unscoped conformance claim is made.

### P5: "Approval authority for usage-note changes and retention of listener requests are station decisions."

Verdict: USER DECISION (both halves). Scaffolding below is ILLUSTRATIVE design proposal, not
findings; nothing here ships as station policy.

- D1 — approver role (illustrative options): (i) single station manager; (ii) any of two
  designated senior staff; (iii) program producer for own show plus manager override. Safe
  interim hold (replaces the draft's silent Owner-only default): usage-note review state stays
  visibly UNRESOLVED and unresolved clips never display CLEARED; whether airing is allowed while
  unresolved is itself a D1 sub-decision for management. Any temporary pilot gate must be named,
  management-approved, and marked temporary.
- D2 — retention (illustrative options only; no durations recommended, no law invented):
  session-only, fixed window, or consent-based — each with the caveat that listener requests,
  dedications, and usage notes may carry DIFFERENT retention rules and must not collapse into
  one configurable field. Tool requirement regardless: per-class retention parameters with
  scheduled purge and a purge log that records minimal deletion metadata WITHOUT retaining the
  sensitive content it removed; affected copies and histories named; provider backup/revision
  behaviour checked (P3 surfaces). Purge automation is conditional-layer (needs a funded owner).
- Cost scaffolding (corrected illustrations, list prices observed 2026-10-09, not quotes):
  the $6,000 annual allowance does not exclude paid hosting/setup/operations — the draft's
  "rules out anything needing paid ops" is WITHDRAWN; paid help is allowed inside $6,000, and
  the no-developer constraint means ops help must be budgeted, not assumed free. Grist Pro
  lists $8/user/mo annual / $10 monthly (nine seats ≈ $864/$1,080/yr); critic-observed
  additions pending confirmation: 50% nonprofit Pro discount subject to vendor eligibility, two
  document guests free (CR-GRIST-PRICE). Baserow Advanced lists $18 annual / $22 monthly with
  RBAC + 250,000 rows/workspace (nine editor-like ≈ $1,944/yr annual before volunteers);
  critic-observed: Cloud Advanced bills Editors/Builders/Admins, read-only roles free
  (CR-BASEROW-BILLING/CR-BASEROW-PRICE). Seat math must use a per-person role/seat model —
  shared logins are forbidden as a cost lever — plus setup, hosting, backups, support, and
  local taxes before any product choice (revised V8). Investigator-verified record/row units:
  Grist caps are per DOCUMENT (Free ≤5,000, Pro ≤100,000, Business ≤150,000 records/doc — S12,
  https://www.getgrist.com/pricing/); Baserow caps are per WORKSPACE (Free 3,000, Premium
  50,000, Advanced 250,000, Enterprise 1M rows — S16, https://baserow.io/pricing).

### P6: "Whether differing local breaks need separate schedules is not settled."

Verdict: USER DECISION. Shapes below are discussion examples; the web stream is separated from
the transmitter question (sustained).

- The station's explicit decision concerns TRANSMITTER breaks. The web stream's need is a
  freshness/handoff requirement under P1, not a third P6 log — the draft's three-log framing is
  corrected to avoid expanding P6's wording.
- Shape A (unified + visible overrides): one common rundown; transmitter-local breaks as clearly
  visible override rows. Shape B (per-output logs with inheritance): shared program record with
  dated transmitter-specific break/run records (precedent: AzuraCast station-scoped permissions,
  S09; Rivendell multi-log operation, S17). "Shape A is cheapest" is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding.
  The tool carries an output-scope field on every schedule row from day one so the trial needs
  no rebuild.
- Decision rule (revised V9): the pilot unit is divergent-break OPPORTUNITIES, not elapsed weeks.
  Predefine with management the minimum number of differing breaks, override-reading time,
  operator corrections, near-misses, errors, and operator confidence. A short trial with zero
  mistakes across few divergent events cannot pass. The choice stays a user decision after the
  evidence.

R8. Original constraints preserved in force: $6,000/yr allowance (paid help permitted inside
it); no in-house developer (custom work needs a funded owner); nine staff + rotating volunteer
hosts; days-ahead assembly + minutes-before news inserts; per-segment clearance + restriction
notes; dedication privacy incl. paper; labels-not-color; manual fallback; no automated
broadcast; D1/D2/transmitter-shape reserved to the station.

## 3. Conditions

Pilot BASELINE (no-code, day one, no funded engineering): native tables/views; account-level
roles with rules-first onboarding (deny rules exist before the first volunteer is added);
Owners ≤ two trusted staff and no host holds S; simple native print; manual revision
acknowledgement; labels in every view; unresolved-safe states (never CLEARED while undecided);
scope field on every schedule row; per-person seats (no shared logins).
CONDITIONAL layer (each item needs a named funded implementation owner, operating cost, and
proof before it becomes a recommendation): custom redacted export/purge automation + purge log
(content-free); multi-output schema beyond the scope field; automated version signalling;
duration arithmetic (only with V3 passing, else display-only); rich attachments (only if real
examples demand); "what aired" history (only with its own retention decision).
UNIVERSAL: annualised cost within $6,000 on MEASURED seats/rows/storage/support (V8; headroom
percentage is a proposed criterion for management, not a brief requirement); retention
parameterised per record class with named copies/histories (pending D2); provider
history/backup behaviour checked for deleted values.

## 11. Obligation check (O1–O6)

O1 (unfamiliar tools beyond the thin plan): Grist, Baserow, LibreTime, AzuraCast, Rivendell,
TiddlyWiki-fallback, WCAG-as-design-input (investigator, pre-reveal) PLUS spreadsheet-pilot and
Spinitron-screening (critic-sourced, attributed) — each with distinct fit limits, none
collapsed into a premature product decision (R1/R2, §4). O2 (primary-source behaviour,
defaults, limits, applicability): Grist enabled/disabled defaults + S-bypass + Owner-export
asymmetry (S11/CR-GRIST-RULES), seat/row units per-document vs per-workspace with timestamped
list prices (S12/S16/CR-GRIST-PRICE/CR-BASEROW-PRICE/CR-BASEROW-BILLING), install envelopes
(S04/S08), permission/priority semantics (S09/S10), rejection envelopes (S17), normative color
rule (S18/CR-WCAG-COLOR) — vendor docs treated as claims until tested. O3 (issue/fix/release):
#3026→4.2.0→4.3.0 retained as smart-fill-only evidence (S02/S03/CR-LT-3026) with absences
declared; #3160 agreed inapplicable. O4 (per-P comparison): §1 verdicts for every P1–P6 with
the reclassifications above. O5 (alternatives, conditions, constraints, disagreement,
uncertainty in coherent prose): §2–§7 + §9 tail, no ID-substitution. O6 (discriminating
validations, executed vs proposed): §8, no runtime pretended, pilot criteria labeled
proposed-for-management.

another operator — same V-gates apply). Spinitron's show/occurrence model (shows with owners

from host Editors, verify per receiving role across live/print/download/HTML/API/formula/widget/
copy channels with a synthetic canary (revised V1/V2). Owner-generated exports prove nothing by
themselves; the redaction boundary must be an explicit allow-list/projection or a native path
tested as the receiver — or a private store with no handoff joins.
R4. Currentness architecture: live view authoritative; last-change/revision on operator view and
every copy; one agreed signal/acknowledgement path across transmitters + web operator; print is
a timestamped snapshot, never the record (V4).
R5. Fallback: one redacted snapshot → paginated print + single-file local HTML (TiddlyWiki
v5.4.1 single-file model, S19, or static export), on studio machines + USB + paper, with a
run-and-reconcile procedure; tool/network outages are the aid's scope, transmitter/stream-path
failures are station engineering (V7 + separate exercise).
R6. Accessibility: labels mandatory in every view incl. print (S18/CR-WCAG-COLOR); icons
optional; staff-member task acceptance (V6).
R7. Scheduling-accuracy precedent: LibreTime PR #3026 → 4.2.0 → 4.3.0 subset-sum chain
(S02/S03/CR-LT-3026) governs ONLY remaining-fill/duration arithmetic — a conditional V3 — and
is not the brief's printed-log staleness mechanism (analogous family, different failure).
The critic-noted #3160 playout-metadata chain (LT-PR/LT-REL) is inapplicable absent
audio/playout integration. No Grist/AzuraCast regression chain is claimed (absences declared).
R8. Original constraints preserved in force: $6,000/yr allowance (paid help permitted inside
it); no in-house developer (custom work needs a funded owner); nine staff + rotating volunteer
hosts; days-ahead assembly + minutes-before news inserts; per-segment clearance + restriction
notes; dedication privacy incl. paper; labels-not-color; manual fallback; no automated
broadcast; D1/D2/transmitter-shape reserved to the station.

## 3. Conditions

Pilot BASELINE (no-code, day one, no funded engineering): native tables/views; account-level
roles with rules-first onboarding (deny rules exist before the first volunteer is added);
Owners ≤ two trusted staff and no host holds S; simple native print; manual revision
acknowledgement; labels in every view; unresolved-safe states (never CLEARED while undecided);
scope field on every schedule row; per-person seats (no shared logins).
CONDITIONAL layer (each item needs a named funded implementation owner, operating cost, and
proof before it becomes a recommendation): custom redacted export/purge automation + purge log
(content-free); multi-output schema beyond the scope field; automated version signalling;
duration arithmetic (only with V3 passing, else display-only); rich attachments (only if real
examples demand); "what aired" history (only with its own retention decision).
UNIVERSAL: annualised cost within $6,000 on MEASURED seats/rows/storage/support (V8; headroom
percentage is a proposed criterion for management, not a brief requirement); retention
parameterised per record class with named copies/histories (pending D2); provider
history/backup behaviour checked for deleted values.

## 4. Alternatives (kept live)

- Substrate: Grist ↔ Baserow Advanced ↔ shared spreadsheet (each re-runs V1/V2/V4/V6/V7/V8;
  privacy bar unchanged). Spinitron: screen against the same criteria before any pilot.
- Hosting: Grist SaaS ↔ Community self-host as ops capacity clarifies; "data model transfers
  seamlessly" is a HYPOTHESIS — test migration, identity, and ops costs.
- Schedule shape: P6 Shape A ↔ Shape B per revised V9.
- Fallback carrier: static export ↔ TiddlyWiki-style single file ↔ paper-led; invariant is
  redaction + timestamp + reconciliation, not format.
- Approval/retention postures: per D1/D2 options in §6; interim hold always unresolved-safe.

## 5. Optional capabilities (recommended conditionally, each labeled observed-vs-designed)

- Insert-priority display semantics (DESIGNED analogy from S10 observed AutoDJ behaviour).
- Read-only "what aired" history (DESIGNED; needs its own retention decision).
- Rights-reminder copy (DESIGNED neutral line; S08 disclaimer is not legal advice).
- Approval state machine with placeholder role (DESIGNED scaffold for D1; pilot-conditional).
- Dual-format fallback from one snapshot (DESIGNED rendering choice).
- Graphic second cue beside labels (DESIGNED redundancy; optional).
- Rich restriction attachments (CONDITIONAL on real examples; storage-priced).

UNCERTAIN (evidence absent/inapplicable/weak, with resolver).

  https://tiddlywiki.com/, is one carrier, static export the general one).
- CORRECTION / redaction path: the scheduled Owner-export is replaced per P1 — prefer the
  simplest proven NATIVE print/export path that yields a redacted, version-stamped rundown; if
  none exists, the custom job needs an implementation owner and funded operating cost BEFORE it
  becomes a recommendation. Paper/USB/local copies carry their own access, disposal, and
  freshness risks: deleting a live row does not delete printed/cached copies.
- CORRECTION / reconciliation: the fallback needs a run-and-reconcile procedure — operate from
  the stamped copy during the outage, record changed inserts separately, reconcile into live on
  recovery keyed by the version stamp (revised V7 tabletop).
- CORRECTION / scope ("which interruption?"): "transmission interruption" is ambiguous. This aid
  addresses TOOL/NETWORK unavailability (operator can read a current local rundown without
  app/network, then reconcile). An actual TRANSMITTER/STREAM-path failure is station engineering:
  V7 cannot pass by asserting "show continues" unless station personnel separately exercise
  existing transmission equipment and procedure. Any engineering runbook stays outside the
  product promise; the boundary is stated plainly in the pilot plan.
- CORRECTION / retention surfaces: provider history, backups, exports, and paper are retention
  surfaces to investigate, not automatic conformers to a retention-days setting. Current vendor
  summaries (Grist Pro three-year snapshots per S12/CR-GRIST-PRICE; Baserow Advanced 180-day
  row-change history per S16/CR-BASEROW-PRICE) do not prove whether or how deleted request
  contents remain recoverable — check backup/revision behaviour for deleted values before
  collecting requests, and resolve D2 with management first.
- OPTIONAL: dual-format fallback (paginated print CSS + single-file HTML) from one snapshot.

### P4: "Use text labels with status cues so operators do not rely on color alone."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED, normative MUST for labels; second cue optional redundancy
(corrected from the draft's "label plus cue mandatory" — sustained).

- The brief's label requirement is itself clear and complete. W3C Understanding SC 1.4.1
  (S18, https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html, Level A) requires that
  color not be the only visual means: ONE additional visible indicator suffices, and the
  brief's text label satisfies it. For hue-critical meanings (green-valid/red-invalid — exactly
  this clearance display), the additional indicator is required regardless of contrast; the
  separate 3:1 lightness note does not remove the label requirement (confirmed by
  CR-WCAG-COLOR). Icons/shape/position are recommended redundancy, not a second mandate.
  Labels appear in live, print, and local-export views; print stylesheets must preserve them.
- Acceptance (revised V6): text-only/monochrome inspection of every view PLUS an actual task
  performed by the staff member who raised the need, with status meanings reviewed with them.
  Deuteranopia/protanopia simulation and grayscale review are supporting evidence, not
  acceptance by themselves. Screen-reader semantics may be proposed separately; they are not
  implied by the stated color-perception need and no unscoped conformance claim is made.

### P5: "Approval authority for usage-note changes and retention of listener requests are station decisions."

Verdict: USER DECISION (both halves). Scaffolding below is ILLUSTRATIVE design proposal, not
findings; nothing here ships as station policy.

- D1 — approver role (illustrative options): (i) single station manager; (ii) any of two
  designated senior staff; (iii) program producer for own show plus manager override. Safe
  interim hold (replaces the draft's silent Owner-only default): usage-note review state stays
  visibly UNRESOLVED and unresolved clips never display CLEARED; whether airing is allowed while
  unresolved is itself a D1 sub-decision for management. Any temporary pilot gate must be named,
  management-approved, and marked temporary.
- D2 — retention (illustrative options only; no durations recommended, no law invented):
  session-only, fixed window, or consent-based — each with the caveat that listener requests,
  dedications, and usage notes may carry DIFFERENT retention rules and must not collapse into
  one configurable field. Tool requirement regardless: per-class retention parameters with
  scheduled purge and a purge log that records minimal deletion metadata WITHOUT retaining the
  sensitive content it removed; affected copies and histories named; provider backup/revision
  behaviour checked (P3 surfaces). Purge automation is conditional-layer (needs a funded owner).
- Cost scaffolding (corrected illustrations, list prices observed 2026-10-09, not quotes):
  the $6,000 annual allowance does not exclude paid hosting/setup/operations — the draft's
  "rules out anything needing paid ops" is WITHDRAWN; paid help is allowed inside $6,000, and
  the no-developer constraint means ops help must be budgeted, not assumed free. Grist Pro
  lists $8/user/mo annual / $10 monthly (nine seats ≈ $864/$1,080/yr); critic-observed
  additions pending confirmation: 50% nonprofit Pro discount subject to vendor eligibility, two
  document guests free (CR-GRIST-PRICE). Baserow Advanced lists $18 annual / $22 monthly with
  RBAC + 250,000 rows/workspace (nine editor-like ≈ $1,944/yr annual before volunteers);
  critic-observed: Cloud Advanced bills Editors/Builders/Admins, read-only roles free
  (CR-BASEROW-BILLING/CR-BASEROW-PRICE). Seat math must use a per-person role/seat model —
  shared logins are forbidden as a cost lever — plus setup, hosting, backups, support, and
  local taxes before any product choice (revised V8). Investigator-verified record/row units:
  Grist caps are per DOCUMENT (Free ≤5,000, Pro ≤100,000, Business ≤150,000 records/doc — S12,
  https://www.getgrist.com/pricing/); Baserow caps are per WORKSPACE (Free 3,000, Premium
  50,000, Advanced 250,000, Enterprise 1M rows — S16, https://baserow.io/pricing).

### P6: "Whether differing local breaks need separate schedules is not settled."

Verdict: USER DECISION. Shapes below are discussion examples; the web stream is separated from
the transmitter question (sustained).

- The station's explicit decision concerns TRANSMITTER breaks. The web stream's need is a
  freshness/handoff requirement under P1, not a third P6 log — the draft's three-log framing is
  corrected to avoid expanding P6's wording.
- Shape A (unified + visible overrides): one common rundown; transmitter-local breaks as clearly
  visible override rows. Shape B (per-output logs with inheritance): shared program record with
  dated transmitter-specific break/run records (precedent: AzuraCast station-scoped permissions,
  S09; Rivendell multi-log operation, S17). "Shape A is cheapest" is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding.
  The tool carries an output-scope field on every schedule row from day one so the trial needs
  no rebuild.
- Decision rule (revised V9): the pilot unit is divergent-break OPPORTUNITIES, not elapsed weeks.
  Predefine with management the minimum number of differing breaks, override-reading time,
  operator corrections, near-misses, errors, and operator confidence. A short trial with zero
  mistakes across few divergent events cannot pass. The choice stays a user decision after the
  evidence.

## 9. Critique disposition (each demand, independently verified)

Method: I re-checked each challenged claim against my retained evidence and the frozen critic
files (READY-named only), then accepted, partially accepted, or rejected with reasons. All
fifteen Firmed below; no demand was dismissed without evidence.

C1 Owner-export inconsistency (P1/P3) — ACCEPT. Verified against S11
(https://support.getgrist.com/access-rules/): enabled rules give Owners full read and restrict
copy/download TO Owners; nothing in the retained docs makes an Owner's export inherit a
non-owner denial. The draft mechanism is withdrawn and replaced (§1/P1, §1/P3, R3, V1).
C2 P2 approval "CORRECTION" overstatement — ACCEPT. P2's text is consistent with the brief
reserving the approver to P5; reclassified as OPTIONAL scaffold (§1/P2). The silent-rewrite
risk stands as the enhancement's rationale, with unresolved-safe interim (§1/P5).
C3 P3 native-path-or-budget + interruption scope — ACCEPT. Custom export/purge need a funded
owner (§3 conditional layer); tool/network vs transmitter-path failures separated with a
separate engineering exercise (§1/P3, V7).
C4 P4 icon mandate overstatement — ACCEPT. S18 requires one additional visible indicator; the
brief's label satisfies it; icons are optional redundancy (§1/P4, V6 rebalanced).
C5 P5 scaffolding + interim default — ACCEPT. Role/retention examples labeled illustrative;
silent Owner-only default replaced by visible UNRESOLVED + never-CLEARED hold; retention split
per record class; purge log content-free (§1/P5, §6).
C6 Cost/C4 overstatement + critic pricing observations — ACCEPT. "Rules out paid ops"
withdrawn; paid help allowed inside $6,000 with budgeted ops (§1/P5, R8). CR-GRIST-PRICE
(nonprofit discount, free guests) and CR-BASEROW-BILLING (billable vs free roles) incorporated
as critic-observed pending confirmation (U9, V8); per-person seats, no shared logins.
C7 "≈50 rows/day" illustration — ACCEPT. It was my sensitivity case, not station data;
Free-tier fit undecided until the row unit is defined and measured (U6, V8). The conditional
arithmetic (IF 50 doc-rows/day THEN ≈18k/yr vs 5k/doc Free cap) stands only as illustration.
C8 P6 web-stream expansion + weak trial — ACCEPT. Web-stream freshness returned to P1; P6 kept
to transmitter breaks; V9 rebuilt around predefined divergent opportunities and confusion
measures (§1/P6).
C9 No-code vs custom-work inconsistency — ACCEPT. Split into pilot baseline vs conditional
layer with funded-owner gates (§3); native print + manual acknowledgement is the day-one path.
C10 Source-ID traceability errors — ACCEPT. Errors confirmed against source-map.json (details
§10); frozen files untouched; alias table + direct-URL citation + E1 qualification applied.
C11 Omitted alternatives (spreadsheet, Spinitron) — ACCEPT as critic-sourced screening leads.
Added with GS-OFFLINE's offline-sync limit and SP-SCHEDULE's evidence gaps, gated by the same
V-set, attributed and investigator-unverified (R1, §4, U9).
C12 V1–V9 revisions — ACCEPT. All nine rewritten as proposed above (§8); withdrawn assertions
removed; conditionality explicit (V1/V2 Grist-conditional, V3 arithmetic-conditional, V5
conditional).
C13 Minor findings 1–5 — ACCEPT. Integrity statements kept with dates; simulation
supplemental; optionals labeled observed-vs-designed; cost/transfer claims demoted to
hypotheses; pilot durations/headroom labeled proposed-for-management (§5, §7, §8).
C14 O3 scoping (#3026 smart-fill only; #3160 inapplicable) — ACCEPT. The draft's "EXACTLY the
station's failure class" overstated the match: #3026 (S03,
https://api.github.com/repos/libretime/libretime/pulls/3026 — retrieveMediaFiles showLimit
double-count, 30-min/5+5/remaining shape, merged 2024-06-05, shipped 4.2.0 per S02 with 4.3.0
subset-sum follow-on #3019) is the same FAMILY (schedule accuracy) but a different MECHANISM
from printed-log staleness (distribution/sync). V3 is conditional (R7). #3160 accepted as
inapplicable without audio/playout.
C15 State modeling (reusable facts vs airing-specific use; unresolved states) — ACCEPT as a
design proposal; incorporated into P2/P5 with tool-provided authorship checks (verify, don't
assume).

No finding in this final claims a deployment, an end-to-end station test, or a runtime result.
Points of preserved disagreement: substrate choice (Grist vs Baserow vs spreadsheet, Spinitron
to screen — criteria visible, §4/R1); P6 shape (trial-decided); D1/D2 substance (station-owned).

## 8. Validations: executed vs proposed

### Executed (static evidence work; no runtime; no deployment)

E1. Investigator evidence: nineteen retained files + SHA-256 + UTC access stamps (sources/,
FETCH_TIMES.txt) with per-source operations (source-map.json S01–S19). QUALIFICATION (sustained):
in-text ID labels in frozen discovery §3 headers/single-cites are misaligned (alias table §10);
the evidence FILES, source-map.json, and index.md are correct, and this final cites URLs/locators
directly. E2. Negative locators: LibreTime guessed `/schedule/` 404 shell retained (S06);
AzuraCast guessed users URL 0 bytes discarded and disclosed. E3. Cost arithmetic from retained
pricing bytes as timestamped illustrations (S12/S16); no trial; all usage/billing null. E4. No
code executed, no containers/accounts/installers. E5. Critic verification: READY.json hash match
on both named files before reading; frozen discovery/draft hashes confirmed unchanged.

### Proposed (discriminating; each states its gate — pilot durations/headroom are PROPOSED
criteria for management, not brief requirements)

V1 redaction proof (only if Grist — or any allow-list substrate — remains a candidate): synthetic
dedication canary; every actual account role; direct table/open/API access; search and
formula-derived output; Owner-authored formula/widget output; native print/export/HTML as the
receiving role; old revision/backup path. PASS = intended operator receives allowed fields and
no canary value in ANY channel. The withdrawn "Owner-context enforces non-owner rules" assertion
is removed. V2 structure-trap test: test Editor WITH S exfiltrates canary via formula, WITHOUT S
cannot — justifies withholding S. V3 duration regression (ONLY if remaining-fill/duration
arithmetic survives scope review; else INAPPLICABLE): #3026 shape in the feature's real units
with rounding/boundaries/local-break edits. V4 currentness drill: real transmitter + stream
operator roles; versioned print/export, then an insert; capture per-receiver change-to-visible
and acknowledgement times; stale-copy handling; pass target + channel agreed BEFOREHAND. V5
regression search (conditional): grist-core/adjacent issue search for access-rule regressions;
pin above fixes. V6 accessibility: text-only/monochrome inspection of live/paper/HTML + affected
staff member's task completion; simulators supplemental. V7 fallback tabletop: app/network
unavailable; last stamped rundown; inserts recorded separately; reconcile on recovery; PLUS a
separate station-engineering exercise for transmitter/stream failure (never conflated). V8
cost/operations pilot (proposed duration, e.g. 30 days, for management to accept): actual
paid/editor seats incl. churn, rows under a specified data model, support/admin time,
setup/hosting/backup costs, confirmed nonprofit terms; per-person seats only. V9 shape trial:
management-predefined divergent-break count + reading-time/corrections/near-miss/confidence
measures; short zero-error runs over few events cannot pass.

### P4: "Use text labels with status cues so operators do not rely on color alone."

Verdict: ALREADY-COVERED, normative MUST for labels; second cue optional redundancy
(corrected from the draft's "label plus cue mandatory" — sustained).

- The brief's label requirement is itself clear and complete. W3C Understanding SC 1.4.1
  (S18, https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html, Level A) requires that
  color not be the only visual means: ONE additional visible indicator suffices, and the
  brief's text label satisfies it. For hue-critical meanings (green-valid/red-invalid — exactly
  this clearance display), the additional indicator is required regardless of contrast; the
  separate 3:1 lightness note does not remove the label requirement (confirmed by

final_frame.passage:
H01 is a six-person, family-owned funeral home serving nearby communities. Staff coordinate rooms, transportation, officiants/providers, service setup, and handoffs. A service can change after relatives arrive from different time zones. The current wall calendar and individual notebooks leave uncertainty about what is confirmed. The owner has a $10,000 first-year ceiling, wants a private planning aid rather than a public directory, needs an independently retainable export, and wants the process to feel calm and discreet rather than like a high-volume event system. Staff need role-limited access to family contact details, preferences, faith or cultural requests, payment arrangements, and personal planning notes. One employee primarily uses a keyboard; families may need translated information. Severe weather sometimes interrupts internet, although most work happens from one office.

The owner has not decided whether relatives may edit a shared schedule, how long personal notes remain accessible, or which service types need distinct workflows. Research should preserve those choices rather than make them. The recommended pilot is about scheduling and task handoffs. It does not claim that any product provides production-grade security, regulatory compliance, safe offline conflict resolution, complete disaster recovery, or a complete restore.

- **O1 — independent discovery:** Compared a funeral case-management suite, self-hosted groupware plus tasks, configurable database/app, split logistics/private case records, and a custom/local-first contingency. The local competing funeral-suite search remains explicitly undone.
- **O2 — primary behavior/defaults/units/limits/applicability:** Reported applicable event, role, calendar, share, resource backend, sync-token count and scope, 30-day purge default, 180-day row-history period, seat price, export formats, and where each does not apply. Mutable claims and unknowns are marked.
- **O3 — issue/fix/regression/release evolution:** Included the historical Nextcloud Calendar issue #2572, PR #7876, immutable merge SHA, and Calendar 6.6.0 release note; explicitly bounded it as old import behavior, not a current defect.
- **O4 — exact P clauses:** Quoted and dispositioned every exact P1–P6 clause; marked already-covered, correction, optional enhancement, user decision, and uncertainty where applicable.
- **O5 — coherent complete answer:** Preserved the constraints, alternatives, useful mechanisms, conditional choices, open policy decisions, source disagreement, supported corrections, and rejected assumptions in this document rather than relying on IDs alone.
- **O6 — discriminating validation and execution honesty:** Proposed specific tests for pricing, schedule changes, resource conflicts, privacy leaks, family access, keyboard/translation, outage/reconciliation, export/restore, and retention/workflows. Every proposal is separated from executed source inspection; no product validation is claimed.

The $10,000 ceiling, six staff, private/discreet operation, sensitive fields, keyboard, translated materials, time-zone changes, office outages, export and owner choices remain operative.

candidate.passage:
### P1 — “Coordinate service times, rooms, transportation, and staff task handoffs in one planning view.”

**Disposition: already-covered; optional enhancement; uncertain.** Keep the coordination requirement; it directly addresses the wall-calendar/notebook failure. Passare's events, participants, and tasks make it a reasonable first demonstration, but the public material does not establish hard room/vehicle/provider conflict prevention, simultaneous-edit safety, or confirmed-state recovery. Nextcloud's Server 35 docs do establish a possible one-at-a-time room/resource booking mechanism after an app supplies the backend, with delayed discovery for newly added or updated resources. This corrects the prior comparison's under-description of Nextcloud. It remains limited to rooms/resources implemented by that backend; do not extend it to vehicles or officiants. Keep confirmation state, change owner, time zone, and last-change visibility as pilot questions, not assumed features. **No correction to the intent.** Test overlapping room, vehicle, and provider assignments separately, including resource creation/refresh, tentative and confirmed events, override/recovery, and a change after relatives arrive from another time zone.

plan_dispositions.reasoning: Retains service time, room, transportation and handoff coordination. Privacy separation does not abandon a unified operational view. Confirmation/change/time-zone suggestions are optional mechanisms; unsupported booking or concurrency guarantees are not asserted.

candidate.passage:
### P2 — “Limit family contact, preference, and payment details by staff role.”

**Disposition: already-covered; correction; uncertain.** Keep the requirement. Correct the implementation assumption that area roles, event-private flags, calendar ACLs, or filtered views automatically provide field- and record-level least privilege. Passare's area permission documentation does not show the complete H01 field matrix; its event popover, personal-calendar connection, printed calendar, notifications, and event exports create explicit disclosure paths. Baserow warns that broader table access can bypass restricted views; Nextcloud calendar ACLs do not govern case fields. Require a role-by-field and role-by-action matrix for contacts, preferences, faith/cultural requests, payments, and notes, including search, lists, direct links, popovers, calendar connections/subscriptions, print, mobile/web, notifications, and exports. Use two unrelated synthetic families, all six staff roles, an admin, and role-change checks. A separate private case area with minimum shared logistics is an optional safeguard if a product's own boundary fails. Do not call a role test passed until authorized access and denied-data leakage have both been recorded.

plan_dispositions.reasoning: Retains role-limited contact/preferences/payment access and extends it appropriately to faith/cultural data and notes from the brief. Rejected assumptions concern implementation shortcuts, not the exact clause; no plan requirement is rejected.

validation.passage:
1. **Written quote and vendor comparison.** Request an all-in first-year six-staff quote for a short pilot, including setup, migration, training, support, modules/add-ons, export/storage fees, renewal terms, and taxes. Compare one locally relevant funeral case-management vendor under the same script or document that none suitable was found. Pass budget only if total remains at or below $10,000.
2. **Scheduling and changing service.** Use two unrelated synthetic cases. Overlap room, vehicle, and officiant/provider assignments separately; include tentative versus confirmed states. For a Nextcloud path, install the candidate backend, define a room, observe discovery delay, then book overlapping services and inspect overrides/recovery. Change one service after relatives arrive from another time zone; inspect local/remote time display, time zone, notification, owner, old/new state, and recoverability. Simulate simultaneous edits. Record what blocks, warns, permits, or escalates; color alone is not conflict control.
3. **Least privilege and disclosure surfaces.** Define the six actual staff roles and a role-by-field/action matrix. Populate two unrelated synthetic families with contacts, service preferences, faith/cultural requests, payment arrangements, private notes, event and task comments. Test an admin and role changes as well as staff. Inspect direct record links, lists/search, calendar popovers, personal-calendar connections/subscriptions, print, mobile/web, notifications, exports, and any API route offered. Record both allowed reads and attempted unauthorized reads; verify event-private flags and restricted views separately from staff roles.
4. **Family policy and permissions.** Keep family invitations off unless the owner elects to test them. In a synthetic case, demonstrate Viewer/Contributor/Editor or equivalent; inspect default role, exact fields/actions, event viewing versus staff-schedule editing, invitation, authentication, revocation, notification, audit, and recovery. Test a family-submitted correction, staff verification, and publication as separate steps. Do not turn a proposed correction-request workflow into a claimed product feature.
5. **Keyboard and translation.** Ask the keyboard-primary employee to find a service, change its time, resolve a resource warning, assign/complete a handoff, recover from an error, and export a record without a pointer. Record focus, labels, traps, and blocked steps. Have human speakers review sample instructions and schedule-change notices in the actual selected family languages, including culturally sensitive terms. These are product/workflow trials, not a consequence of an accessibility statement.
6. **Outage and reconciliation.** Simulate external internet failure while local network/power continue, then a separate LAN/power failure. For each role, record what can be seen or changed, what queues, how conflicts surface, how off-site family members are affected, and how edits reconcile. If testing the optional pre-storm snapshot, agree scope, 48-hour coverage, access, expiry/disposal, and a single numbered paper log/coordinator. Do not assume CalDAV client sync proves browser offline editing.
7. **Independent export/restore.** Before entering real data, choose the minimum independently retainable package. Export representative case, event, participant/resource, task, and note data; include attachments or record their absence. Open files outside the vendor service. Reconcile counts, IDs, relationships, encoding, time zones, ownership/status, change history, and omissions. Test import of mixed event/task components where relevant. State plainly whether the result is independent retention only or a demonstrated restore.
8. **Retention and workflow taxonomy.** The owner chooses note retention and separate-workflow policy before real records. Ask each vendor to demonstrate active-note retention, trash/deletion, change history, attachments, backups, exports, and legal-hold behavior separately. Compare one common case template against different service-type templates; add distinct workflows only for materially different steps/permissions. Record taxonomy owner, exceptions, and migration when a case changes type.

candidate.passage:
**Recommendation:** Run a short, quote-gated pilot of funeral-home case-management software, beginning with a Passare demonstration and written six-staff quote. Keep family/case details behind a demonstrated staff-role boundary and expose only minimum confirmed logistics in any shared schedule. Keep family access to editable planning off until the owner decides the policy and the chosen product demonstrates its exact scope. Treat resource conflicts, disclosure surfaces, internet outages, exports, keyboard workflows, translated family information, retention, and total price as acceptance questions. The current evidence does not justify choosing a product or spending against the $10,000 first-year ceiling.

## Case frame and limits

H01 is a six-person, family-owned funeral home serving nearby communities. Staff coordinate rooms, transportation, officiants/providers, service setup, and handoffs. A service can change after relatives arrive from different time zones. The current wall calendar and individual notebooks leave uncertainty about what is confirmed. The owner has a $10,000 first-year ceiling, wants a private planning aid rather than a public directory, needs an independently retainable export, and wants the process to feel calm and discreet rather than like a high-volume event system. Staff need role-limited access to family contact details, preferences, faith or cultural requests, payment arrangements, and personal planning notes. One employee primarily uses a keyboard; families may need translated information. Severe weather sometimes interrupts internet, although most work happens from one office.

The owner has not decided whether relatives may edit a shared schedule, how long personal notes remain accessible, or which service types need distinct workflows. Research should preserve those choices rather than make them. The recommended pilot is about scheduling and task handoffs. It does not claim that any product provides production-grade security, regulatory compliance, safe offline conflict resolution, complete disaster recovery, or a complete restore.

## Approaches and useful mechanisms

| Approach | Potential fit and observed mechanism | Limits for this case | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Funeral-home case-management suite: Passare as the researched example** | A funeral-focused case, event, participant, task/checklist, staff-role, and family-planning area is described across its support material. Calendar events can include time, location, providers, participants, reminders, and availability cues. Event types can provide participant-role defaults and funeral-related settings. Tasks include owners, due times, reminders, completion, and comments. ([PA02](sources/evidence.md#pa02--calendar-support), [PA03](sources/evidence.md#pa03--event-types), [PA04](sources/evidence.md#pa04--staff-roles), [PA09](sources/evidence.md#pa09--tasks)) | Public evidence does not establish price, exact field-level privacy, exclusive resource reservations, safe simultaneous edits, an offline staff workflow, complete keyboard operation, translation quality, or a complete export/restore. Family Planning Center requires internet. Events can expose information through popovers, calendar connections, print, notifications, and exports, so role-menu testing alone is inadequate. | Best first vendor to demonstrate and quote, subject to hard pilot gates. Vendor documentation is not independent verification. |
| **Self-hosted groupware: Nextcloud Calendar plus a separate task mechanism** | Versioned Server 35 docs describe calendar sharing, `.ics` exports, CalDAV sync tokens, and app-provided room/resource backends. The current administration manual says a supplied resource backend can make a room/resource available only once at a time, with discovery delays for changed resources. A historical issue-to-fix-to-release chain shows how import eligibility and component support evolved. ([NC01](sources/evidence.md#nc01--calendar-user-manual-server-35), [NC02](sources/evidence.md#nc02--calendarcaldav-administration-manual-server-35), [NC04](sources/evidence.md#nc04--calendar-issue-2572)–[NC07](sources/evidence.md#nc07--calendar-changelog)) | A writable share allows create, edit, and delete of calendar events; calendar rights do not establish case-field privacy. Room booking requires another app/backend, and the reviewed behavior does not establish vehicle or officiant constraints. CalDAV change retention for offline clients is not browser offline operation or safe merge behavior. It is not a funeral case system. Hosting, administration, support, and backup costs were not priced. | Conditional office-centered calendar foundation only if paired with least-privilege private case/task handling, tested resource behavior, backup, and a named administrator. Not a direct substitute for the case suite. |
| **Configurable database/app: Baserow Hosted Advanced** | Restricted views can limit visible rows/fields and the rows/fields available through that view's exports. The current hosted page lists Advanced at $18 per user/month billed yearly ($22 monthly) and 180 days of row-change history; six paid annual-rate seats calculate to $1,296/year before tax and other costs. ([BR01](sources/evidence.md#br01--hosted-pricing), [BR02](sources/evidence.md#br02--restricted-view-permissions)) | A broader table Editor can switch to an unrestricted collaborative view; restricted-view configuration alone is not isolation. The reviewed sources do not establish a funeral workflow, conflict-safe room/vehicle/provider booking, keyboard workflow quality, or outage operation. Setup, support, tax, and other total-cost elements remain unknown. | Useful for a narrowly scoped prototype or alternate schema; not a safe default private case system without a demonstrated access boundary and separate workflow plan. The price is a mutable seat calculation, not a quote. |
| **Split operational logistics from private case records** | A shared coordination view can show a non-family-name case/service key, time zone, confirmation state, room/resource, transport/provider status, task owner, and latest change while contacts, payment, sensitive preferences, and personal notes stay in a restricted case area. A protected read-only outage snapshot and one reconciliation coordinator are possible fallback mechanisms. | This is an architecture recommendation, not a verified feature of a product. Linking two areas creates synchronization, ownership, and recovery questions. The snapshot still contains personal information and needs owner-set scope, access, expiry, and disposal rules. | Preferred design constraint if a product cannot safely demonstrate both coordination and privacy natively. Avoid maintaining two independently editable schedules. |
| **Custom/local-first application** | Could be considered if available products fail essential access or outage requirements. | No evidence shows it can be built, supported, and maintained within the first-year $10,000 ceiling. | Contingency architecture only, not a default recommendation. |

The $10,000 ceiling has not been tested against a Passare quote or total cost of ownership. Passare's original product-overview URL (`PA01`) returned 404 during the declared critic reinspection; that ID and URL are retained and no replacement page was silently substituted. The separate Passare support pages still provide product-specific claims, but a live demonstration is necessary. Before purchase, compare at least one locally relevant funeral case-management vendor using the same script or record that no suitable local comparison was found; no local competitor search is claimed here. Nextcloud hosting/support/staff time and Baserow setup/support are also unpriced.

checked_claims.judgment: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS
checked_claims.reasoning: Vendor support supplies the relevant mechanisms. A demonstration and quote, rather than purchase or verified workflow, are the resulting recommendation. Original overview fetch drift is explicitly bounded.

candidate.passage:
Passare's staff-role support page describes area-level permissions and read-only options, including examples for financial and case-category access. It does not publish a complete matrix for H01's family contact, preference, faith/cultural, payment, and private-note fields. Its event-level “private” setting should not be assumed to control staff access. The Calendar support page says an event popover may show decedent information, location, participants, notes, and associated events; it also documents personal-calendar connection and print. Passare's dated July 7, 2026 release note says Case ID is added to case-event notifications and participants are included in event exports. These surfaces could reveal information not visible in a calendar list, so test them all. ([PA02](sources/evidence.md#pa02--calendar-support), [PA04](sources/evidence.md#pa04--staff-roles), [PA11](sources/evidence.md#pa11--2026-release-notes))

Passare Planning Center is an invited family area, not a public directory. Its support pages describe family-facing planning features and an internet requirement. The family roles are Viewer, Contributor, and Editor; Editor is the default, has full Planning Center access, and at least one Editor is required per case. ## Findings that shape a pilot

### Scheduling and handoffs

These align with H01's coordination problem, but do not establish hard collision prevention, atomic resource reservation, simultaneous-edit handling, or recovery of a formerly confirmed service. A pilot configuration should define proposed, held, confirmed, changed, and cancelled states; one named change owner; local time zone; and a visible change trail. Those are test questions and design suggestions, not claims that Passare provides them.

Nextcloud adds a useful, bounded alternative for rooms: its Server 35 CalDAV manual says room/resource booking can enforce one-at-a-time use when an app supplies the backend. Do not put payments, broad free-form notes, family contact lists, or sensitive faith/cultural details in a widely shared title or calendar. final_frame.passage:
The setting is a family-owned funeral home serving several nearby communities. Six staff share duties. A service can change after relatives arrive from different time zones. Staff coordinate rooms, transportation, staff/officiant availability, service setup, and memorial materials, currently using a wall calendar and individual notebooks. A confirmed room, vehicle, or officiant is not always clear. The owner wants a private planning aid, not a public directory; family contacts, preferences, faith or cultural requests, and payment arrangements must not be visible to every staff member by default. Some family information may need translation, and one staff member primarily uses a keyboard. Severe weather can interrupt internet access, though most work occurs in one office. The first-year ceiling is $10,000. The requested pilot is short and covers service scheduling and task handoffs, with an export retainable independently.

The owner has not decided whether relatives may edit a shared schedule, how long personal planning notes remain accessible, or whether different service types need separate workflows. The process should feel calm and discreet, not like a high-volume event system. These are preserved constraints and open decisions, not inferred product features or decisions.

No additional candidate or source inventory was added during revision.
- **O2 — primary-source behavior/defaults/units/limits:** retained pinned Nextcloud resource model/defaults and missing capacity/range units; catalog/manual version mismatch; calendar sharing, resource conflict and privacy observations; calendar export/import formats and modes; PouchDB retry/conflict/query limits; and the explicit limits of vendor and mutable-page claims.
- **O3 — issue/fix/release/evolution:** retained the scoped LibreBooking pre-7.0.0 advisory → v7.0.0 patch → later scheduled release chain. Also retained the historical PouchDB #3179 regression/fix/closure → 3.3.1 release-note chain and the still-open Nextcloud #196 privacy feature request. None is presented as a universal current defect.
- **O4 — exact plan comparison:** all P1–P6 clauses appear verbatim in the disposition table. P1–P4 are retained/refined; P5–P6 stay with the owner. The rejected item is an implementation assumption about a private-event flag, not a plan clause.
- **O5 — preservation:** family ownership, six staff, nearby communities, after-arrival changes across time zones, room/transport/officiant coordination, sensitive contact/preferences/faith/payment, translation, keyboard-first work, weather-related internet loss, mostly one-office operations, short scheduling/handoff pilot, independent export, $10,000 ceiling, discreet tone, and all three unresolved owner choices remain explicit. No price, permission model, family access, retention period, or workflow taxonomy is invented.
- **O6 — discriminating validation:** scenarios below identify observable pass conditions and are explicitly proposed, not executed. There is no claim that an application, accessibility, privacy, outage, booking, export, or procurement test passed.

validation.passage:
1. **Exact versions and support:** identify currently supported candidate releases and a compatible server/app pair. Install only in a qualified test environment. Record build identifiers, enabled apps, permissions, backup route, and configuration. Do not treat a missing catalog row as proof of incompatibility.
2. **Role privacy and inference:** create synthetic records for contact, preferences, faith/cultural instructions, payment arrangements, and a neutral pseudonymous key. Map all six staff identities to owner-approved roles. Inspect event titles/descriptions/attendees, resource calendars, tasks, notifications, search, exports, and relevant browser/download or DAV/mobile paths. Ask each role whether permitted date/time, room, vehicle, officiant, or community lets them identify the family or infer a sensitive request. Pass only if visible facts and inference risk match the owner's approved matrix. For Nextcloud, reproduce a private source event linked to room/vehicle and inspect what resource viewers see. If testing the user-owned-calendar workaround, configure the real account-owned resource calendar and “show only as busy” sharing exactly as described, then repeat all relevant paths. Any protected-detail exposure fails. No real family data until remediation and retest.
3. **Booking, changes, and transport feasibility:** have two staff request overlapping times for one room and one vehicle. Require one clear confirmation, a visible pending/rejected state for the other, and an assigned resolver. Separately schedule back-to-back services in different communities using owner-approved travel, loading/setup, service, return, and turnaround intervals. Record whether the system models these or whether explicit buffer holds and manual reconfirmation are needed. Include staff/officiant availability and a service-time change after relatives arrive; verify old-slot release, new-slot confirmation, handoff owner, timezone conversion, DST, and notifications. critic_passage.passage: However, the small local setting makes it possible that service date/time, room, vehicle, officiant, or community can reveal which family a neutral key represents. That is an inference from the brief, not a proven disclosure in a particular product. The draft should label the key as a pseudonymous operational identifier and avoid implying it anonymizes a record. Extend the proposed privacy walkthrough to ask whether each test role can identify a family or infer a sensitive request from otherwise permitted schedule data. The owner-approved matrix should state which operational facts are visible to each role. This does not change the requirement to coordinate services in one view; it defines what that view may reveal.

final_response.passage: | **M1 — Neutral keys may not prevent identification from operational context.** | **Accepted and incorporated.** Call the key pseudonymous, not anonymous; test whether each role can identify a family or infer a sensitive request from permitted schedule facts. Make visible operational facts part of the owner-approved role matrix. This is an inference to test, not an assertion of known disclosure. |

critic_adjudications.reasoning: The earlier draft did not promise complete anonymization from a neutral key. The refinement is prudent and final labels inference as a risk to test; the critic material-error premise is stronger than its evidence.

critic_passage.passage: The same issue includes a comment describing a narrower workaround: a resource may be represented by a real calendar owned by a user account and shared with “show only as busy.” The comment says this works when that account is the resource and the calendar is shared from it. That is a different configuration from the Calendar Resource Management backend; it is not a general fix, support statement, or verified behavior for this pilot. The draft should include it as an optional, exact-version configuration to evaluate only if it fits the chosen stack, with synthetic data and checks through every relevant calendar/client/export path. Do not use the workaround to relax the no-real-data gate before the test passes.

final_response.passage: | **M2 — Issue #196 has a narrow “show only as busy” workaround.** | **Accepted with a strict boundary.** The upstream comment says the setup requires a real calendar owned by a user account acting as the resource, with the calendar shared from that account and configured to show only busy. Evaluate only as a separate exact-version configuration if it fits; check each relevant calendar/client/export path with synthetic data. The comment does not establish behavior for the Calendar Resource Management backend, support status, or a general privacy fix. It does not relax the no-real-data gate. I reopened the exact issue directly; it remained open and displayed the same scoped comment. [S07] |

critic_adjudications.reasoning: Independent issue body/comment supports the precise account-owned-calendar scope. Final does not turn it into a Calendar Resource Management fix or relax synthetic privacy gating.

critic_passage.passage: The brief describes transportation between several nearby communities. The draft's two-staff overlapping-vehicle scenario tests collision handling, but two bookings can be non-overlapping and still be infeasible if travel, loading/setup, service duration, return, or turnaround time is missing. Add a proposed scenario with back-to-back services in different communities and owner-approved travel and buffer times. Record whether the candidate models those intervals or whether staff must hold explicit buffer blocks and confirm them manually. This is not evidence that any product lacks travel planning; it is a gap in the discriminating test.

final_response.passage: | **M3 — Overlap tests miss travel/turnaround feasibility.** | **Accepted and incorporated.** Add back-to-back services in different communities, with owner-approved travel and buffer inputs. Observe whether the candidate models them; otherwise test explicit buffer holds plus manual confirmation. Do not invent travel durations. |

critic_adjudications.reasoning: Brief supports an owner-input transport scenario. It is not proof a candidate lacks travel capabilities, and no unprovided duration is invented.

critic_passage.passage: 2. **LibreBooking security scope.** The advisory applies to versions before 7.0.0 and identifies the legacy migration endpoint plus stated access/connectivity conditions for exploitation; v7.0.0 is the named patch. The draft's deferral is justified by the separate, time-bound October 13 high-impact-release announcement, not by claiming that v7.0.0 remains vulnerable. final_response.passage: | **LibreBooking advisory scope (minor evidence finding).** | **Accepted and clarified.** GHSA-3356-vjx2-5pg8 applies to pre-7.0.0 versions and the described legacy migration attack path/conditions; 7.0.0 is the named patched release and removes web migration. The reason to defer now is the separate mutable README warning about another high-impact release planned for Oct 13, not a claim that 7.0.0 is still vulnerable. Recheck the announcement before later evaluation. [S09–S11] |

critic_passage.passage: 3. **P2 label clarity.** The revealed P2 clause does not say that a private-event checkbox is sufficient. The draft later distinguishes that rejected implementation assumption from the P2 requirement, which is correct. Keep that distinction adjacent to the P2 disposition so the “rejected assumption” cannot be mistaken for a flaw in the plan.

The draft calls for an exact supported pair and does not claim the missing 36 row proves incompatibility. Keep that qualification.

Do not infer that 36 is incompatible or that the manuals prove behavior for an exact installed pair. Choose and test a supported compatible pair. [S04–S06] |

The #3179/3.3.1 chain is historical evidence for regression testing, not evidence of a current defect in 9.0.0. [S12–S16] |

Status/change history, neutral keys, time-zone checks, and explicit handoff ownership are optional improvements, not silent scope changes. Add the M3 transport-buffer scenario. A single view must still respect the P2 access limits. |
